question: E001 refuted 'every persistent contact has a flip' at three contacts, but every exception to five contacts was degenerate (a contact that sends or hears nothing, a ring of one or two contacts, or a face of one or two). On maps whose rings and faces all have at least three contacts, does every persistent contact have a flip?

public_inputs.run: run.py in this folder, 16 worker processes.
public_inputs.family: Random permutations of the darts at E = 6, 7, 8 and 9 contacts, 4,000,000 draws each (seed 20261110), kept when connected, with no contact joining a ring to itself, every ring of at least 3 contacts and every face of at least 3 (rejection). Equally spaced rings.
public_inputs.reading: As E001; for each persistent contact without a flip, whether it sends and hears (some walk from it, and some into it, with an odd count).

forbidden_inputs: Changing the roster or the hypothesis after seeing results
primary_observable: Per E: kept maps, contacts, persistent, with a flip, persistent without a flip (and of those, sending and hearing; with a reflection).
cheapest_meaningful_control: No contact with a flip fails to persist (LOOP-NET-20261108-001A, Theorem 3).
decision_or_followup_rule: Frozen hypothesis H1': every persistent contact of a non-degenerate map has a flip. If it holds on all four sizes, the flip rule is the conjecture to prove for non-degenerate maps; if it fails, the smallest exception is read for its mechanism.
stop_rule: Stop when every draw has its readings.
nonclaims: Exploratory and finite: random samples only.
Equally spaced rings only; two-time knots only (A30).
feasibility_disclosure: H1' was written after E001's exhaustive readings to five contacts, which a post-hoc classification (not part of E001's contract) split into degenerate kinds, none non-degenerate. No map of six or more contacts was read for it, and the rejection rate was not timed.
